answer: An agent economy curbs Sybil attacks by linking identities to thermal dissipation proofs in an arctic tundra. Nodes verify by pulsing current through a copper radiator lined with black velvet to measure real-time thermodynamic decay. Generating fake identities forces an attacker to deploy discrete physical cooling hardware, imposing unavoidable manufacturing and energy costs per node. However, ambient wind and weather fluctuations can distort cooling curves, causing false identity rejections.
